rows.name: Qur'an
rows.detail: Partnership recognized, not legislated: 38:24 ('many partners wrong one another') and 4:12 ('partners in a third'). Root SH-R-K.
rows.detail_long: The Qur'an assumes partnership as social fact — Dawud's parable of wronging partners (38:24) and the inheritance rule making heirs 'partners in a third' (4:12) — without legislating its contract law.

rows.timeline_year_basis: no app dating block — 610 period fallback
rows.name: Sunan Abi Da'ud 3383
rows.detail: Hadith qudsi: 'I am the third of two partners as long as neither betrays the other.'
rows.detail_long: Allah declares Himself the third of two honest partners, withdrawing when one cheats. Grading is disputed (a little-known narrator in the chain; al-Hakim graded it sahih; the app file's own status is Sahih). The Prophet also confirmed pre-Islamic partnerships that continued into Islam.
rows.internal_ref: Record + grading pulled from app hadith file (kafalah_source_extract.json session)

rows.name: Bulugh al-Maram 1013
rows.detail: 'I am the third of two partners'. The qudsi charter of partnership: 'I am the third of two partners as long as one does not cheat the other; if he cheats, I depart.'
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim (Abu Hurairah): Allah declares Himself the third partner of any two honest partners, withdrawing when either cheats. The moral warranty clause of every shirkah — trust is the capital that keeps God in the venture.
rows.evidence_display: Bulugh al-Maram 1013 (text + dating block in app)
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch2_source_extract_new.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Sunan Ibn Majah 2287
rows.detail: Partner of the Prophet before Islam. Al-Sa'ib to the Prophet: 'You were my partner in the Ignorance period, and the best of partners — you did not contend or dispute.'
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: partnership predates revelation; the Prophet himself traded as a partner before prophethood and is praised for how he behaved in it. Da'eef in the app — kept as colour on continuity of the institution, not as proof.

topics_app: Partnership in Farming with Taxpayers and Others and Conditions Between Them

rows.detail: Farming partnership chapter. Imam al-Sadiq permits a farming partnership with a non-Muslim — land/seed/bull from one side, labour from the other, produce split — and polices which side owes which input.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: the questioner provides land, seed and bull; the non-Muslim partner works the farm; after the ruler's levy, produce splits one-third / rest. 'It is not unlawful.' When the questioner wants seed repaid off the top, the Imam corrects him: the partnership he formed obliges HIM to provide the seed. Capital-labour partnerships arrive with input obligations already itemised.
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch2_source_extract_new.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Ibn Abbas (attrib., Tanwir al-Miqbas)
rows.detail: The earliest attributed gloss on 38:24: 'many partners oppress one another — save those who believe and do good, and they are few.'
rows.detail_long: Tanwir al-Miqbas (in the app) on the Dawud verse reads khulata' as partners 'and brothers' who 'transgress against one another', excepting the believers who deal rightly — 'those who do not transgress' being few. The Qur'an's own risk warning about partnership, and its exception clause. Attribution traditional, not critical — hence 'attrib.'
rows.evidence_display: Tanwir al-Miqbas (attrib. Ibn Abbas), on Q38:24 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app tafsir file (batch2_source_extract_new.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Ibn Kathir
rows.detail: Ibn Kathir on 38:24: strips the Dawud story of Isra'iliyat embellishment — source criticism applied to the partnership verse itself.
rows.detail_long: The app's Ibn Kathir passage on 38:24 (read this session) declines the popular back-story: 'mostly based upon Isra'iliyat narrations. Nothing has been reported about this from the Infallible Prophet that we could accept as true', and grades the one Hadith chain as weak. What survives scrutiny is the verse's own rule — partners wrong each other, except the believers who do right.
rows.evidence_display: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, on Q38:24 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app tafsir file (batch2_source_extract_new.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: al-Qurtubi
rows.detail: Al-Qurtubi discusses co-mingling (khultah) and its rules on 38:24 and 4:12.
rows.detail_long: Al-Qurtubi's treatments of 38:24 (16,200 chars) and 4:12 (9,700 chars) in the app work the partnership rules latent in both verses — the wronging partners of Dawud's parable, and the heirs made 'partners in a third' — the co-mingling (khultah) discussion jurists cite for shirkah.
rows.evidence_display: al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an, on Q38:24 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim this session from app tafsir file (batch2_source_extract.json)

rows.name: al-Sarakhsi
rows.detail: Al-Sarakhsi splits shirkah into ownership vs contract partnership, with subtypes 'inan, mufawada, abdan, wujuh.
rows.detail_long: The Mabsut's fourfold typology — equal-liability mufawada, limited 'inan, labor partnership abdan, credit partnership wujuh — is the classification every later school text and modern standard inherits. App book F0333-B50.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.3; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.name: al-Kasani
rows.detail: Al-Kasani completes the Hanafi doctrine of partnership types.
rows.detail_long: Bada'i refines the conditions of each shirkah type and the profit/loss rules. Finance-local figure.

rows.name: Ibn Rushd
rows.detail: Ibn Rushd supplies the comparative four-school picture of shirkah.
rows.detail_long: Bidayat al-Mujtahid maps where the schools agree and split on partnership — the comparative lens modern standard-setters still use. App book F0751-B51.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.3; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.name: Mohammad Nejatullah Siddiqi
rows.detail: 'Diminishing musharakah' engineered for home finance — the ideal profit-and-loss alternative to interest.
rows.detail_long: Siddiqi and colleagues design the declining-balance partnership: bank and customer co-own the house, the customer buys the bank's share out over time while paying rent on the remainder — now the flagship Islamic mortgage.

rows.name: Industry practice
rows.detail: Small in practice: 0.8% of 2022 sukuk issuance vs wakala 27.3%, murabaha 24.8% (IFSB 2023).
rows.detail_long: Held up as the 'ideal' profit-and-loss mode, musharakah remains a sliver of actual volume — the theory-practice gap critics of the industry point to first.
